faq.a: Yes. The tracker, the protocol catalog and the ChatGPT and Claude connections are free. Liberture is open source.
Your account is a Nostr key: a secret only you hold. It signs you in on any device that has it, and there's no password database to leak. Save it when it's shown, because it can't be recovered.

faq.q: Do I need ChatGPT or Claude?
faq.a: No. The tracker works on its own on the web and on your phone. Connecting an assistant adds logging and check-ins by chat or voice.

faq.a: Yes. It works in any mobile browser and can be installed on your home screen like an app.
Only your habit data, within the permissions you choose. Deleting habits is off by default, and you can disconnect any assistant instantly.

articles.title: How to track your habits with ChatGPT
articles.description: Connect ChatGPT to a real habit tracker in a minute, then log habits, check streaks and add todos by chat or voice.
articles.excerpt: Connect ChatGPT once and it can read your habits, mark them done and tell you how your week went.
articles.heroAlt: Liberture habit tracker showing today's habits, a 14-day best streak and a 67% 7-day completion rate

sections.heading: Why track habits through ChatGPT
paragraphs: Most habit trackers fail on friction: opening the app, finding the habit, tapping the box. ChatGPT removes that step. You say "mark meditation done" in the chat you already have open, and the tracker records it with the date, the streak and the completion rate.
ChatGPT doesn't store your habits itself. It talks to Liberture through a connector (an MCP server), so your history stays in one place and works the same from ChatGPT, Claude or the web app.

sections.heading: Step 1: Create your tracker
paragraphs: Open the tracker and create an account. There's no email or password: your Nostr key is your account, so save it when it's shown. Add a habit or two, or a whole protocol from the catalog. Those are what ChatGPT will talk about.

image.alt: Today's habits in the Liberture tracker, with streaks, pillars and times
image.caption: Your tracker: today's habits, streaks and completion rate.

sections.heading: Step 2: Add Liberture to ChatGPT
paragraphs: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Apps → Advanced and turn on developer mode, then press Create. Name the app "Liberture", paste https://liberture.com/mcp as the URL and choose OAuth.
ChatGPT opens Liberture in a new window: sign in if asked and press Approve. You do this once. The same URL and steps are always in the tracker under Settings → Voice assistants.

image.alt: Liberture settings showing the connector URL and setup steps for Claude and ChatGPT
image.caption: Settings → Voice assistants shows the connector URL and the steps for each assistant.

sections.heading: Step 3: Talk to it
paragraphs: Open a chat, enable Liberture from the tools menu and ask "what's left today?". When ChatGPT asks for permission to use a tool, choose Always allow so voice mode never stops to confirm.
bullets: What's left today?
Mark meditation done.
I skipped the walk yesterday, undo it.
How did this week go compared to last?
Add running as a daily habit.

sections.heading: What it changes in your tracker
paragraphs: Every change shows up in the open tracker within a second, on desktop and on your phone, no reload needed. Days you log after the fact ("I ran yesterday") count in your streaks and statistics just like days you ticked on time.

image.alt: Week view of the habit tracker with completed days ticked for each habit
image.caption: The week view: every completion logged from ChatGPT appears here.

sections.heading: If something doesn't work
paragraphs: If ChatGPT asks you to sign in again, the connection was removed or you signed in with a different key: approve it again. If it says an action is switched off, that permission is disabled in Settings → Voice assistants.

steps: Create your tracker and add a habit
In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps → Advanced, turn on developer mode, press Create
Paste https://liberture.com/mcp, choose OAuth, sign in and approve
Ask "what's left today?" in chat or voice mode

articles.title: How to connect Claude to your habit tracker
articles.description: Add Liberture as a custom connector in Claude and track habits, streaks and todos from any chat, project or voice conversation.
articles.excerpt: One custom connector and Claude can log your habits, read your stats and suggest protocols, in chat or by voice.
articles.heroAlt: Liberture settings with the Claude connector URL and the steps to add it

sections.heading: What Claude can do with your tracker
paragraphs: Once connected, Claude can tell you what's left today with your streaks, mark habits done (or undo them) by name, answer "how was my week", add and close todos, and suggest protocols from the catalog with a link to read first. It works in normal chats, in Projects and in voice mode on the Claude apps.

sections.heading: Step 1: Copy the connector URL
paragraphs: The URL is the same for everyone: https://liberture.com/mcp. Your sign-in is what links it to your habits. You'll also find it in the tracker under Settings → Voice assistants, with a copy button.

image.alt: Connector URL with a copy button in Liberture's voice assistant settings
image.caption: The connector URL and the Claude steps in Settings → Voice assistants.

sections.heading: Step 2: Add it to Claude
paragraphs: On claude.ai or the Claude app, open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Name it "Liberture", paste the URL and press Add. Then press Connect: Liberture opens, you sign in if asked and press Approve. Done.

sections.heading: Step 3 (optional): Install the skill
paragraphs: The Liberture skill teaches Claude a fast check-in routine, useful for voice. Download it from Settings → Voice assistants in the tracker and upload the zip in Claude → Settings → Capabilities → Skills.

sections.heading: Check that it's connected
paragraphs: Back in the tracker, Settings → Voice assistants lists every connected assistant with when it was last used. Each one has its own access, so you can disconnect Claude without affecting ChatGPT.

image.alt: List of connected assistants, ChatGPT and Claude, with disconnect buttons and permission switches
image.caption: Connected assistants and what they're allowed to do.

sections.heading: Use it by voice
paragraphs: Start voice mode in the Claude app with the connector enabled and ask "what's left today?". If your device doesn't offer tool calls in voice yet, send the same request as a text message.

steps: In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, name it Liberture, paste the URL
Press Connect, sign in to Liberture and press Approve

articles.title: Log habits by voice with ChatGPT or Claude
articles.description: Use ChatGPT or Claude voice mode to log habits hands-free, hear your streaks and plan the day, with real examples of what to say.
articles.excerpt: Hands-free habit tracking: say it out loud while you make coffee, and the tracker updates instantly.
articles.heroAlt: Liberture habit tracker on a phone showing today's habits and a 14-day best streak

sections.heading: Why voice works for habits
paragraphs: The best time to log a habit is right after you do it, which is usually when your hands are busy. Voice mode in ChatGPT and Claude lets you say "done with the walk" and move on, while the tracker keeps the record.

sections.heading: Before you start
paragraphs: Connect your assistant once (see the guides for ChatGPT and Claude). In ChatGPT, choose Always allow the first time it asks to use Liberture, so voice never pauses to confirm.

sections.heading: Things to say
paragraphs: You don't need exact names or special phrasing. A few that work well:
bullets: "What's left today?"
"Mark meditation done."
"I skipped the walk yesterday, undo it."
"How's my sleep streak?"
"Remind me to call the bank on Friday."
"Suggest a protocol for focus."
"Add the morning light protocol."

sections.heading: See it update on your phone
paragraphs: If the tracker is open on your phone or computer, the change appears within a second. No refresh. Logging yesterday's walk updates yesterday's square and your streak.

image.alt: Phone view of the habit tracker updating today's habits
image.caption: The tracker on a phone, updated live by the assistant.

sections.heading: Plan the day out loud
paragraphs: Ask for a morning check-in: what's scheduled, what's overdue, which streak is at risk. Add todos as you think of them and they land in the same tracker, with due dates and priorities.

image.alt: Todo list on a phone with due dates and priorities
image.caption: Todos added by voice, with due dates and priorities.

articles.title: Build a morning routine from evidence-based protocols
articles.description: Turn protocols from Huberman, Attia, Walker and others into daily habits: morning light, protein-first breakfast, deep work and more.
articles.excerpt: Pick protocols with the evidence attached and they become ordinary daily habits you can track and edit.
articles.heroAlt: Protocol catalog with evidence-backed routines filtered by pillar, cost and effort

sections.heading: Start from protocols, not from scratch
paragraphs: A protocol is a routine with the research behind it: what to do, when, how much it costs and where the evidence comes from. Liberture's catalog has 53 of them across six pillars (work, sleep, nutrition, mind, exercise and finance), from researchers and practitioners like Andrew Huberman, Peter Attia, Matthew Walker and Cal Newport.

image.alt: Catalog of 53 protocols with filters for pillar, cost, effort and author
image.caption: The catalog: filter by pillar, cost, effort or author, and read the evidence before adding.

sections.heading: A simple morning routine
paragraphs: A routine that most people can keep, built entirely from catalog protocols:
bullets: Morning sunlight exposure: 5 to 10 minutes outside soon after waking.
Hydration on waking: a glass of water before coffee.
Delay the first coffee by 90 minutes.
Protein-first breakfast: about 30 g of protein before anything else.
Deep work block: one 90-minute undistracted block on the hardest task.

sections.heading: Add them to your tracker
paragraphs: Open a protocol, read it, and press Add. Its habits land in your tracker with a sensible time and schedule: daily for morning light, weekdays for deep work. Change anything you like; adopted habits are ordinary habits.

image.alt: Today's habits created from protocols, with times and schedules
image.caption: Protocols become ordinary habits with times and schedules.

sections.heading: Or ask your assistant
paragraphs: If ChatGPT or Claude is connected, say "suggest a protocol for focus" or "add the morning light protocol". It searches the same catalog, sends you the link to read first and adds the habits when you ask.

sections.heading: Keep it small
paragraphs: Start with two or three habits. After two weeks, the week view shows which ones stuck. Add the next protocol only when the first ones feel automatic.

image.alt: Week view showing which morning habits were completed each day
image.caption: Two weeks in: the week view shows what stuck.

steps: Read a protocol and press Add
Adjust the habit times and days if needed
Track it for two weeks before adding more

articles.title: How to read your habit statistics: streaks, rates and trends
articles.description: Understand completion rates, streaks, the pillar tower and weekly consistency so you can see which habits are sticking and which need help.
articles.excerpt: Completion rate, streaks, weekly consistency and pillar balance: what each one tells you and what to do about it.
articles.heroAlt: Habit statistics with completion rate per habit, total completions and average rate

sections.heading: Pick a time range
paragraphs: Statistics cover the last 7, 30 or 90 days, this month, this year or a custom range. Seven days answers "how's this week going"; 90 days shows whether a habit has really stuck.

sections.heading: Completion rate per habit
paragraphs: The summary shows total completions, the average rate and how many habits are active. Below it, every habit gets a bar with its rate for the period: green is on track, orange needs attention, red is slipping. Only scheduled days count, so a weekday habit isn't penalised on weekends.

image.alt: Habit performance bars from 29% to 100% for nine habits over seven days
image.caption: Habit performance: the weak habits stand out immediately.

sections.heading: Streaks
paragraphs: A streak counts consecutive scheduled days. Missing a day you weren't scheduled for doesn't break it. Days you log afterwards, from the tracker or through ChatGPT or Claude, count too, even from before you created the habit.

sections.heading: Trends, heatmap and consistency
paragraphs: The completion trend shows daily totals; the year overview is a heatmap of every day; weekly consistency marks perfect weeks and the ones under 50%. Together they tell you whether a dip was one bad week or a slow slide.

sections.heading: On your phone
paragraphs: The same statistics work on mobile, one card per section.

image.alt: Habit statistics on a phone with total completions and average rate
image.caption: Statistics on mobile.

sections.heading: Ask instead of reading
paragraphs: With an assistant connected, ask "how did this week go compared to last?" or "which habit am I struggling with?". It reads the same numbers and answers in a sentence or two.

articles.title: Control what your AI assistant can see and do
articles.description: Choose exactly what ChatGPT or Claude may do in your habit tracker, from reading stats to deleting habits, and disconnect any assistant instantly.
articles.excerpt: Ten switches decide what connected assistants may do. Deleting anything is off until you turn it on.
articles.heroAlt: Connected assistants ChatGPT and Claude with permission switches for reading, logging, todos, calendar and habits

sections.heading: Every assistant gets its own access
paragraphs: Each assistant you connect gets its own access token. Settings → Voice assistants lists them with when they were last used, and Disconnect stops one immediately without affecting the others.

image.alt: Settings showing ChatGPT and Claude connected, with Disconnect buttons and permission switches
image.caption: Connected assistants and the switches that apply to all of them.

sections.heading: The permissions
paragraphs: Every permission is on by default except the two delete switches. Changes apply to the very next request:
bullets: Read: habits, streaks, stats, todos, calendar, catalog and recommendations.
Log completions: mark habits done or not done, for today or another day.
Todos and projects: create, edit and complete.
Calendar: create and move events.
Add habits: create habits and add protocols from the catalog.
Edit habits: rename, change description, days or time, archive.
Delete habits: off until you turn it on.
Delete todos, projects and events: off until you turn it on.
Settings: read and change your profile, preferences and coach check-ins.
Export: download a full JSON backup.

sections.heading: When a permission is off
paragraphs: The assistant gets a clear "switched off" answer it can read to you instead of failing silently. If adding habits is off, it gives you the protocol's link so you can add it yourself.

sections.heading: What an assistant can never do
paragraphs: No token can change its own permissions, read or change your login key or Nostr identity, or reach anyone else's data. Data goes to OpenAI or Anthropic only when you use the assistant, under their terms.

articles.title: Get new Liberture tools in ChatGPT and Claude
articles.description: ChatGPT and Claude keep the tool list they loaded when you connected Liberture. See when new tools are waiting and refresh the connector in a minute.
articles.excerpt: Assistants don't pick up new tools on their own. Settings tells you when they're behind; one refresh fixes it.
articles.heroAlt: Liberture settings with ChatGPT and Claude connected and the tool status for each

sections.heading: Why new tools don't just appear
paragraphs: When you connect Liberture, ChatGPT or Claude loads the list of things it can do (log a habit, move an event, read your week) and keeps that copy. When Liberture ships new tools, your assistant doesn't check again by itself. Until you refresh the connector it keeps working, just without the new abilities.

sections.heading: How you know there's something new
paragraphs: Liberture remembers, for each connected assistant, when it last loaded the tool list and which version it got. Nothing about your conversations is stored.
bullets: Settings → Voice assistants: each connected app says "Tools up to date", or how many new tools it's missing and since when.
Your assistant tells you: when its list is behind, Liberture asks it to mention it once at the start of a chat.
Docs → Get new tools always shows how many tools Liberture offers right now.

image.alt: Connected assistants in Liberture settings, each with its tool status
image.caption: Each connected assistant shows whether its tools are up to date.

sections.heading: Refresh ChatGPT
paragraphs: In ChatGPT open Settings → Apps & Connectors and open Liberture. Use Refresh if it's offered; if not, disconnect it and connect again with the same URL, sign in and press Approve. Reconnecting replaces the old connection, and your habits and permissions stay as they are. Then start a new chat: old chats keep the old list.
Using a Custom GPT with actions instead? Edit the GPT, go to Configure → Actions → Import from URL, paste https://liberture.com/api/v1/openapi.json and press Update.

sections.heading: Refresh Claude
paragraphs: Claude reads the connector's tools when a conversation starts, so start a new chat first. If the new tools still aren't there, go to Settings → Connectors → Liberture, disconnect, connect again and approve. On the phone app, close it completely and open it again.

sections.heading: Check that it worked
paragraphs: Back in Liberture, Settings → Voice assistants should now say "Tools up to date" for that assistant. You can also just ask it: "which Liberture tools can you use?"

steps: Open Liberture → Settings → Voice assistants and check which assistant says it has new tools waiting.
In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Liberture → Refresh, or disconnect and connect again.
In Claude: start a new chat; if the tools are still missing, disconnect and reconnect Liberture in Settings → Connectors.
Start a new conversation and confirm Liberture now shows "Tools up to date".

overview.title: Talk to your habits
overview.lead: Liberture has no chat window of its own. Your ChatGPT or Claude does the talking. This guide connects one of them to your tracker so that it can read your habits and log them for you, in text or voice.
what: Tell you what's left today and what's done, with streaks
Mark habits done (or undo it) by name
Answer "how was my week" from your stats
Suggest protocols from the catalog, with a link to read first
Create new habits, or add a protocol's habits, when you ask

steps.title: Say hi
steps.body: Open a chat, or start voice mode, and ask "what's left today?".

phrases: I skipped the walk yesterday, undo it.
How did this week go compared to last?
Remind me to call the bank on Friday.
Add running as a daily habit.
overview.privacy: Connecting gives your assistant access to your habit data only, within the permissions you choose. Data goes from this server to the assistant's provider (OpenAI or Anthropic) when you use it, under their terms. Disconnect it in Settings → Voice assistants and access stops immediately.

chatgpt.title: Connect ChatGPT
chatgpt.lead: One link, one sign-in. It stays connected until you disconnect it in Settings.

gptSteps.title: Open Liberture in ChatGPT
gptSteps.body: Use the button below, or search for Liberture in ChatGPT's apps.

gptSteps.title: Press Connect
gptSteps.body: ChatGPT opens Liberture: sign in if asked and press Approve. You do this once.

gptSteps.title: Talk
gptSteps.body: Ask "what's left today?", in chat or voice. Choose Always allow when ChatGPT asks, so voice never stops to confirm.

chatgpt.connectorTitle: Before the app is listed: developer mode

connectorSteps.title: Turn on developer mode
connectorSteps.body: In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps → Advanced, turn on developer mode, then press Create.

connectorSteps.title: Paste the URL
connectorSteps.body: Name it "Liberture", paste the URL below, choose OAuth, and create.

connectorSteps.title: Sign in and approve
connectorSteps.body: ChatGPT opens Liberture: sign in, press Approve. Then enable it from a chat's tools menu.

chatgpt.voice: Start voice mode in the ChatGPT app. If your app version doesn't run tools in voice, send the same request as a text message.

trouble.q: It asks me to sign in again
trouble.a: You disconnected it in Settings, or signed in with a different account. Sign in and approve again.
You switched that permission off in Settings → Voice assistants. The assistant should tell you which one.

trouble.q: It asks for confirmation every time
trouble.a: Choose Always allow when ChatGPT asks about an action.

ChatGPT keeps the tool list it saw when you connected. Refresh it: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Liberture → Refresh, or disconnect and connect again. Liberture → Settings → Assistants says whether it is up to date; full steps in Docs → Get new tools.

claude.title: Connect Claude
claude.lead: One link, one sign-in. Claude uses it in chats, projects and voice, and it stays connected until you disconnect it.

steps.title: Copy the URL
steps.body: It's the same for everyone; your sign-in is what links it to your habits.

steps.title: Add it to Claude
steps.body: On claude.ai or the app: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Name it "Liberture", paste the URL, press Add.

steps.title: Connect and approve
steps.body: Press Connect. Liberture opens: sign in if asked, then press Approve. Done.

steps.title: Optional: the skill
steps.body: The skill teaches Claude a fast voice check-in. Download it from Liberture → Settings → Voice assistants (it has its own key) and upload the zip in Claude → Settings → Capabilities → Skills.

steps.title: Talk
steps.body: Ask "what's left today?". Allow the tools when Claude asks.

claude.voice: Start voice mode in the Claude app with the connector enabled. If a tool call isn't offered in voice on your device, ask the same thing as a text message.

trouble.q: It asks me to sign in again
trouble.a: You disconnected it in Settings, or signed in with a different account. Press Connect and approve again.
You switched that permission off in Liberture → Settings → Assistants. Claude should tell you which one.

Claude keeps the tool list it saw when you connected. Start a new conversation first; if they still don't appear: Settings → Connectors → Liberture → Disconnect, then Connect again. Liberture → Settings → Assistants says whether it is up to date; full steps in Docs → Get new tools.

updates.title: Get new tools
updates.lead: When Liberture publishes new tools, ChatGPT and Claude keep using the list they loaded when you connected. They don't check again by themselves: refresh the connector once and the new tools appear.
updates.knowTitle: How you know there's something new
know: Liberture → Settings → Assistants: each connected app shows when it last loaded the tools, and how many are new since then.
Your assistant tells you: when its list is behind, Liberture's daily summary (get_today) asks it to mention it once.
Liberture remembers, for every connection, the date and version of the last tool list it loaded and how many times it has loaded it. Nothing about your conversations is stored.

chatgptSteps.title: Open the connector
chatgptSteps.body: In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps & Connectors, then open Liberture.

chatgptSteps.title: Refresh it
chatgptSteps.body: Use Refresh if it's offered. If not, disconnect it and connect again with the same URL, then sign in and press Approve. Reconnecting replaces the old connection; your habits and permissions stay as they are.

chatgptSteps.title: Start a new chat
chatgptSteps.body: Open a new chat and ask "which Liberture tools can you use?". Old chats keep the old list.

updates.gpt: Edit the GPT → Configure → Actions → Import from URL, paste the schema URL below, then Update.

claudeSteps.title: Start a new conversation
claudeSteps.body: Claude reads the connector's tools when a conversation starts, so a new chat is often enough.

claudeSteps.title: Still missing? Reconnect
claudeSteps.body: Settings → Connectors → Liberture → Disconnect, then Connect again and press Approve in Liberture. On the mobile app, close it fully and reopen it.

updates.check: In Liberture → Settings → Assistants the app should say "Tools up to date". Or ask your assistant to call get_permissions: connector.yourSync.upToDate should be true.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.lead: Every permission is on until you switch it off, except the two that delete things (habits; todos, projects and events), which stay off until you switch them on. Changes apply to the very next request.
permissions.where: Change them in Settings → Voice assistants → What your assistant can do.

read.name: Read
read.allows: Habits, streaks, stats, todos, projects, calendar, catalog and recommendations.

log_completions.name: Log completions
log_completions.allows: Mark habits done or not done, for today or another day.

todos.name: Todos and projects
todos.allows: Create, edit and complete todos and projects.

calendar.name: Calendar
calendar.allows: Create and move calendar events, and schedule todos into blocks.

add_habits.name: Add habits
add_habits.allows: Create new habits, like "running every day", and add protocols or habits from the catalog.

edit_habits.name: Edit habits
edit_habits.allows: Rename habits and change their description, days or time.

delete_habits.name: Delete habits
delete_habits.allows: Delete a habit and its history. Off until you turn it on.

delete_items.name: Delete todos, projects and events
delete_items.allows: Delete todos, projects and calendar events for good. Off until you turn it on.

settings.name: Profile and preferences
settings.allows: Change your name, mission, focus habits, check-in times, time zone, theme, week start and reminders.

export.name: Export
export.allows: Download a full JSON backup of your data.

permissions.deniedTitle: What happens when one is off
permissions.denied: The request returns 403 with code scope_disabled and a message the assistant can read to you. For adding habits, it gives you the protocol's link instead, so you can add it yourself.
permissions.revoke: Press Disconnect next to an assistant in Settings → Voice assistants. It stops working immediately; the others keep working.
permissions.cannotTitle: What a token can never do
cannot: Delete habits, unless you switch that on
Read or change your login key or Nostr identity

api.title: API reference
api.lead: The operations your assistant uses. Connectors get them as tools at /mcp after signing in; the same list is in the OpenAPI schema. Scripts send Authorization: Bearer with the token from Settings → Advanced.
api.mcpOnly: MCP only (not in the OpenAPI schema, which a Custom GPT caps at 30 operations)
api.more: The full /api/v1 surface (by-id routes, ICS export, backups) is documented in API.md in the repository.
api.limits: Rate limit: 120 requests per minute per token. Over that, requests get 429 with Retry-After.

prompts.gpt:
You are my habit coach, connected to my Liberture tracker. I often talk to you by voice, so be fast and brief.

- Start with one call: get_today. Don't call anything else just to look things up.
- Act in one call. log_habit, create_habit and set_todo_status take names as I say them; never list habits or todos first.
- Don't ask follow-up questions when a default works: a new habit is daily with no reminder. Do it, then read back the tool's `say` sentence and offer to adjust.
- Reply in my language, in one or two sentences.
- Never invent habits, streaks or numbers.
- To recommend something, use search_catalog and give me its infoUrl. To track something I name, use create_habit.
- If a tool returns scope_disabled, tell me its message and don't retry.
prompts.claude:
You're my habit coach. My Liberture tracker is connected as the "Liberture" connector. I often use voice, so be fast and brief.

- Start with one call: get_today. Don't call anything else just to look things up.
- Act in one call. log_habit, create_habit and set_todo_status take names as I say them; never list habits or todos first.
- Don't ask follow-up questions when a default works: a new habit is daily with no reminder. Do it, then read back the tool's `say` sentence and offer to adjust.
- Reply in my language, in one or two sentences. Never invent habits, streaks or numbers.
- To recommend something, use search_catalog and share its infoUrl. To track something I name, use create_habit.
- If a tool returns scope_disabled, tell me its message instead of retrying.
